It's something far more serious: pathological calcification.

This is where calcium starts building up where it shouldn't, not just in your arteries, but inside your cells and soft tissues. We're talking about your brain, your eyes, your kidneys, and even your heart.

Here's why this happens: Magnesium is the master controller of other minerals, especially calcium. It's what keeps calcium from accumulating excessively in your cells. Too much calcium is toxic — it can actually kill the cell. The right balance of calcium is only good for you if you have enough magnesium to regulate it.

videos.title: The Worst Time to Brush Your Teeth | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
The Worst Time to Brush Your Teeth | Dr. Mandell Most people brush their teeth every day without giving a second thought to when they should brush. But did you know that brushing immediately after eating certain acidic foods and beverages may actually do more harm than good? In this video, I explain why timing matters, how acidic foods can temporarily soften tooth enamel, and why your body's own saliva plays such an important role in protecting and remineralizing your teeth. We'll discuss which foods and drinks are the biggest culprits, what you should do immediately after eating them, and why waiting about 30 minutes before brushing may help protect your enamel for years to come. This isn't about brushing less—it's about brushing smarter. Understanding how your body naturally protects itself allows you to make better health decisions every day. In this golf lesson, I’ll show you what that mistake is, why it can rob you of strike and speed, and then give you 3 simple golf tips you can practice for just 2 minutes each to start changing the way your body, arms and club work together.

• Why trying too hard to hit the ball then the ground can actually make your golf swing worse

• The common movement pattern I saw across 196,000 golf swings

• How to stop pushing everything forward through impact

• A simple “throwing water” feel that can help your body move more naturally

• The longest chip drill I use to help golfers blend the body and arms together

• Why you shouldn’t have to consciously release the golf club

• How a ball in a sock or towel can help you feel a freer, more powerful golf swing

• How to combine all 3 drills into a simple 6-minute daily practice routine

07.08.26 - Rift Education Day RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.summary_source_text:
Learn To Balance In Your Punch Turns The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: This Popular Drink Could Be Clogging Your Arteries | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
This Popular Drink Could Be Clogging Your Arteries | Dr. Mandell This popular drink may seem harmless—or even healthy—but when it’s loaded with added sugar, drinking it day after day can contribute to metabolic changes that affect your heart and arteries. In this video, I explain what can happen inside your body when you regularly consume sugar-sweetened tea and other sugary beverages, including how excess sugar can affect insulin, triglycerides, inflammation, body fat, cholesterol, and the delicate lining of your blood vessels. We’ll discuss why liquid sugar can be so easy to overconsume, why a drink labeled “tea,” “natural,” or even “organic” isn’t automatically healthy, and why reading the added-sugars line on the nutrition label is so important. You’ll also learn how years of repeated metabolic stress can contribute to the conditions that promote plaque formation within the arteries, even when you feel perfectly healthy and have no obvious symptoms. Most importantly, I’ll show you simple ways to continue enjoying tea without loading your body with unnecessary sugar, including gradually reducing sweetness, mixing sweetened and unsweetened tea, and using natural flavors such as lemon, lime, mint, or cinnamon. Heart disease doesn’t develop because of one drink or one meal—it develops from patterns repeated over time. Becoming aware of what you drink every day may be one of the simplest changes you can make to support healthier arteries, better metabolism, and a stronger cardiovascular system for years to come.

videos.summary_source_text:
I Built a Local AI Cluster and My AI Agents Are Free Now 🐝 Join the community where all of this is running: https://mrc.fm/cmc

I built a local AI cluster out of Macs I already owned, and my AI agents now run for free, with no API key and no bill. This is Buzz Shared Compute: run an LLM locally, share it with your community, and point your AI agents at a machine in someone else's house instead of OpenAI or Anthropic.

Everything here runs on a Mac Studio M3 Ultra, a Mac mini and a MacBook Pro: a local LLM cluster, self-hosted AI, zero cloud spend. Underneath it is the open-source MeshLLM project, which Block shipped into Buzz at the end of July. I show the full setup end to end, then the catch nobody mentions: the person whose machine answers your prompt can read what you sent it.

10:20 Should You Turn It On?

🖥 THE HARDWARE IN THIS VIDEO
Mac Studio M3 Ultra 256GB · Mac mini · MacBook Pro M1 Max 24GB
Models: Gemma 4 26B, Gemma 4 E4B, Llama 3.3 70B

⚠️ THREE GOTCHAS
1. Sharing is Mac only at time of filming. Windows and Linux can use the pool but not lend to it. Check your own build.
2. There's an open bug where the toggle sits on "starting" forever.
3. Don't pick the biggest model your machine can hold. Take the recommendation. Reasoning models burn tokens thinking and your agent feels sluggish.

06.08.26 - Rift Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Do This If Your Struggle To Increase Rotation In Hockey The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Strong Breathing Muscles = Longer Life?
videos.summary_source_text:
Strong Breathing Muscles = Longer Life? You've probably heard that VO2 max is one of the strongest predictors of health span and longevity. While your heart plays a central role, VO2 max also depends on your lungs, blood, muscles, and the strength and endurance of your breathing muscles.

The best way to improve VO2 max is through regular aerobic exercise, especially vigorous exercise. But if you're unable to train hard, or you simply want to strengthen your breathing muscles, inspiratory muscle training can be a useful supplement.

There are many resistance breathing devices on the market, but they need to be cleaned carefully because moisture can allow bacteria and mold to grow. That's why I like using a simple aluminum straw. It's inexpensive, easy to disinfect, and can provide breathing resistance without the maintenance challenges of more complex devices.

This kind of alternative is great for developers, startups, and anyone looking to run a self-sovereign AI workforce under their own control.

One of the earliest warning signs of heart problems can be erectile dysfunction. It often appears 3 to 5 years before heart disease because the blood vessels that supply an erection are narrower, so problems tend to show up there first.

If you have erectile dysfunction or other warning signs of heart disease, the following tests can help assess your heart health:

• CAC (coronary artery calcium) test
• Ultrasound of the carotid arteries
• Fasting insulin test

If you still get erections during the night or early morning, you may not have a vascular problem. 

Testosterone drives libido, not the erection itself. Nitric oxide plays an important role in healthy erectile function, but nitric oxide levels naturally decline with age. Poorly controlled blood sugar, smoking, vaping, sleep apnea, chronic inflammation, certain medications, and a sedentary lifestyle can also decrease nitric oxide.

If you have erectile dysfunction or any other warning signs of heart disease, it’s important to discuss them with your doctor.

videos.title: 05.08.26 - Ep.20 (Part 2) - Autonomous Capital Allocation
videos.summary_source_text:
05.08.26 - Ep.20 (Part 2) - Autonomous Capital Allocation In this continuation of RIFT Before You Quit – Episode 20, the focus shifts from trading individual assets to understanding how professional institutions manage capital at scale. Rather than asking "What should I buy?", the world's largest investment firms ask a far more important question: "How should capital be allocated?"

The session explores why allocation, diversification and risk management are the true foundations of long-term wealth creation, and how artificial intelligence is transforming these processes.

Topics covered include:

- Why professional investors focus on capital allocation rather than individual trades.
- How AI continuously rebalances portfolios based on changing market conditions.
- The importance of position sizing, diversification and adaptive portfolio management.
- How institutional capital rotates between stocks, commodities, bonds, crypto, real estate and cash.
- Understanding Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT), diversification, correlation, Sharpe Ratio, Beta, volatility clustering and risk-adjusted returns.
- Why institutions build portfolios for consistency and resilience instead of chasing maximum returns.
- How RIFT's AlphaFlow, SmartFlow and MicroFlow represent different participation environments designed around continuous market engagement.
- Why AI is designed to complement human decision-making rather than replace it.
- How machine learning relies on high-quality financial data including price action, order books, liquidity, portfolio history and behavioural patterns.
- The role of trading books as complete records of portfolio management rather than simple trade histories.
- How Mirror Wallet infrastructure creates valuable behavioural data that continuously improves AI models.
- The evolution from trading signals, copy trading and mirror trading towards intelligent Smart Money infrastructure and AI-powered participation networks.
- How behavioural analysis contributes to the development of Capital Identity and future reputation-based financial systems.
- The long-term vision for RIFT as an integrated AI-powered financial ecosystem combining Smart Money, automated trading, portfolio intelligence and adaptive capital management.

The presentation also examines how global financial institutions such as BlackRock, Bridgewater, Goldman Sachs and Renaissance Technologies increasingly rely on AI, mathematics and engineering to manage capital more efficiently than traditional discretionary approaches.

Finally, the episode looks ahead to the future of finance, discussing autonomous capital allocation, AI-native financial infrastructure, tokenised assets, digital identity and self-learning financial systems, while previewing the next stage of the Before You Quit series, where intelligent market infrastructure and prediction markets will be explored in greater depth.

Whether you are an experienced trader or simply interested in where financial technology is heading, this episode provides valuable insight into how AI is reshaping modern portfolio management and why understanding capital allocation may become one of the most important skills in tomorrow's financial world. videos.summary_source_text:
Demidov’s Punch Precursor The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

More than 50% of adults in the United States have high blood pressure, and many don’t know it. High blood pressure is often called the “silent killer” because it can go undetected.

Research has shown that the wall sit is one of the best exercises to help reduce systolic blood pressure. A wall sit is an isometric exercise, meaning your muscles contract without movement.

The wall sit exercise can lower systolic blood pressure by about 8 points, outperforming many other forms of exercise. If you have high diastolic blood pressure, cardio exercise may be more beneficial.

Reducing high blood pressure may also lower your risk of:
• Cardiovascular events
• Coronary heart disease
• Stroke
• Heart failure
• All-cause mortality

To help support healthy blood pressure levels, perform 4 wall sits in a row, holding each for 2 minutes with a 2-minute rest between each set. Repeat this routine 3 times per week.

04.08.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

• AI-Powered Trading Tools

Activate This Muscle To Avoid Slipping The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Why Does McDavid Strides Wide? The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

If you want to get 6 pack abs, there are a few things you need to get right. In this video, I’m breaking down 13 of my best tips for getting six pack abs by combining smarter nutrition, better ab workouts, and more effective exercise technique. You cannot build a visible, ripped six pack by focusing on ab exercises alone. You need to train the muscles correctly while also lowering body fat through a sustainable nutrition plan.

The first tip starts where your day begins. After going several hours without water while you sleep, you may wake up mildly dehydrated. Drinking 16 to 20 ounces of water shortly after waking can help you rehydrate before training, eating, or starting the rest of your day. Proper hydration supports exercise performance, energy, and the quality of your ab workouts. Whether your goal is to lose belly fat or perform better in the gym, staying hydrated matters.

Next, pay attention to the order of your ab exercises. Start with lower ab exercises that require you to move the legs or pelvis. These movements are often more demanding and require greater control. Save top-down movements, such as crunch variations, for later in the workout. This lets you perform the hardest exercises while your abs are fresh and your form is still strong.

When it comes to nutrition for six pack abs, use a simple plate strategy to control portions without counting every calorie. Imagine your plate as a clock. Fill the largest portion with fibrous carbohydrates such as vegetables. Fill the next largest portion with a quality source of protein. Use the smallest section for starchy carbohydrates, then include a modest amount of dietary fat. This makes it easier to build balanced meals and stay consistent with your fat loss goals.

For a complete list of better carbohydrate choices, visit https://athleanx.com/carbs.

During your ab workouts, stop focusing only on how many reps you complete. Make every repetition count. A fast, careless rep that creates little tension in the abs should not count the same as a controlled contraction. Slow the movement down and focus on feeling the abdominal muscles do the work. Quality contractions will do more for building defined abs than racing through sloppy repetitions.

On lower ab exercises, think about lifting the pelvis rather than simply lifting the legs. Moving the legs without curling the pelvis can allow the hip flexors to take over. When possible, squeeze the knees together to engage the adductors. This can improve pelvic stability and create a stronger contraction in the lower abs.

For upper ab exercises, imagine a line running across the bottom of your ribcage. Try to fold your torso over that line. Focus on lifting the shoulder blades off the floor by contracting the abs instead of pulling on your head or neck. This can make top-down ab exercises safer and more effective.

Your diet can also include a few simple additions that may support fat loss when used consistently. Green tea, cinnamon, and red pepper flakes are easy additions. I personally use Ceylon cinnamon in oatmeal and red pepper flakes in different foods throughout the day. None of these will give you abs by themselves, but small habits can support a stronger nutrition plan when combined with training, calorie control, and consistency.

Breathing is another important part of ab training. If you push your abdomen outward every time you exhale, you may reinforce a distended appearance through the midsection. Instead, tighten the waist by engaging the transverse abdominis as you breathe out. Think about drawing the abdomen inward while maintaining control of the movement. With practice, this can become automatic and improve your control of the core.

The rest of the 13 tips for getting 6 pack abs are covered in the video. Watch the full breakdown and let me know which tip helped you most.

Getting abs is not about finding one magical exercise or following an extreme diet. It comes from combining effective ab workouts, better technique, proper hydration, smart food choices, portion control, and a plan you can follow long enough to see results. The goal is not simply to lose weight. It is to reduce body fat while building strong, visible abdominal muscles.

Most golfers trying to square the club face are working on the wrong part of the swing. Eric Cogorno and Golf Digest Top In State instructor Steve Sieracki break down why club face control and casting problems almost always start at setup — and how two specific positions, the elbow squeeze and forearm rotation, fix both at the same time. Get the elbows in the three position at setup, maintain that radius through the ball, and add the forearm pronation to keep the face closed to the shaft — and solid contact with a predictable draw becomes the natural result. These are the same golf impact position keys Eric uses at his golf schools to fix slicers and golfers who can't stop casting. If you leave this video without trying the radius drill, you're leaving solid contact and club face control on the table.

What You'll Learn:
• Why squeezing the elbows together at setup is the first step to fixing golf impact position
• How the radius — left arm and shaft alignment — controls contact and prevents casting in the golf swing
• The three position: elbows squeezed, arms straight, butt of club ahead of the leading edge with shaft lean
• The fist and a half checkpoint for correct hand distance from the body at setup and follow through
• How forearm rotation in the golf swing — right forearm pronation — keeps the face closed to the shaft
• Why twisting the face closed with the elbow still forward is the key indicator of ball striking ability
• How Golf Digest Top In State instructor Steve Sieracki teaches club face control for a draw and predictable ball flight
• How keeping setup and follow through positions the same creates repeatable contact and predictable curve

videos.title: 03.08.26 - Ep.20 - The AI Capital Manager
videos.summary_source_text:
03.08.26 - Ep.20 - The AI Capital Manager In Episode 20 of RIFT Before You Quit, the series moves into one of the most important developments in modern finance: the rise of AI Capital Managers and the growing role of artificial intelligence in managing wealth.

For decades, successful investing was believed to depend on experience, intuition and human judgment. Today, financial markets are changing. Institutions are increasingly relying on artificial intelligence, quantitative models and automated systems that can process millions of pieces of market data every second, helping them make faster, more disciplined and more consistent decisions than any individual trader.

This episode explores why the financial industry is moving away from emotion-driven decision making and toward machine-assisted capital management. Rather than focusing on predicting the next winning trade, modern AI systems concentrate on managing portfolios, controlling risk, preserving capital and continuously adapting to changing market conditions.

You'll discover why firms such as BlackRock, Renaissance Technologies, Two Sigma, Citadel Securities and JP Morgan invest billions into AI research and why platforms such as BlackRock's famous Aladdin system have become some of the most influential pieces of financial infrastructure ever created.

Topics covered include:

• Why artificial intelligence is becoming the future of capital management
• The evolution from human intuition to AI-driven investing
• How institutional investors differ from retail traders
• Human psychology versus machine discipline
• Behavioural finance and the biases that damage investment performance
• Loss aversion, confirmation bias, overconfidence, recency bias and FOMO
• Why institutions focus on probability rather than prediction
• How AI continuously monitors portfolios instead of individual trades
• The difference between trading and professional capital management
• Why portfolio health is more important than finding the next winning trade
• How AI analyses thousands of market variables simultaneously
• Portfolio optimisation and continuous risk assessment
• Why hedge funds increasingly hire engineers, mathematicians and data scientists instead of traditional traders
• Inside BlackRock's Aladdin portfolio management system
• Scenario analysis and institutional stress testing
• Correlation, diversification and intelligent capital allocation
• Why modern finance has become an engineering discipline
• How probability-based investing outperforms emotionally driven decision making over the long term
• The growing role of autonomous capital allocation

Throughout the presentation, the discussion reinforces a key theme running throughout the RIFT Before You Quit series:

Professional trading is not about making perfect predictions. It is about building systems that consistently manage risk, preserve capital and make better decisions over time.

The episode also explains how these institutional concepts relate to the wider RIFT ecosystem, where users are introduced to machine-assisted trading tools, automated trading environments and professional portfolio management concepts designed to encourage disciplined participation rather than emotional speculation.

As the financial industry moves toward AI-assisted decision making, understanding how intelligent systems analyse markets may become just as important as understanding the markets themselves.

Episode 20 will continue by introducing the next major topic in the episode: Autonomous Capital Allocation—how AI systems determine where capital should be deployed, how they balance growth and risk, and why autonomous portfolio management could become one of the defining technologies of the next generation of finance.

Whether you're interested in cryptocurrency, futures, AI, portfolio management or the future of financial technology, this episode provides valuable insight into where institutional finance is heading—and why intelligent infrastructure may become the greatest competitive advantage of the next decade. videos.title: After Injury: How Soon to Exercise Again?
videos.summary_source_text:
After Injury: How Soon to Exercise Again? The answer is: not today, but also not too long.

For most minor injuries, you want to get back to movement once the initial inflammation settles and you have a better idea of what you're dealing with.

As a general rule, if discomfort is around 4/10 or less, careful movement is often appropriate:

Walking
Gentle strengthening
Controlled stretching

Movement during recovery can help restore function and provide the mechanical loading that supports collagen remodeling and better tissue organization as you heal. 💪

The goal isn't to push through pain. It's to get moving again without waiting until you feel 100%. The answer is: not today, but also not too long.

If you leave this video without trying the radius drill, you're leaving solid contact and club face control on the table.

• The three position: elbows squeezed, arms straight, butt of club ahead of the leading edge with shaft lean

• How keeping setup and follow through positions the same creates repeatable contact and predictable curve

videos.title: The "Inner Spring" That Makes McDavid's Stride Effortless
videos.summary_source_text:
The "Inner Spring" That Makes McDavid's Stride Effortless How McDavid Gets Free Speed From His Muscles

There is a kind of speed that costs you almost nothing to produce, and most players never tap into it because they try to generate everything with raw muscle instead. The clue shows up in a simple test. Take the exact same athlete and have them jump one way that removes the little dip beforehand, then jump again using a quick countermovement first, and the second jump is meaningfully higher despite the identical effort, typically by somewhere in the range of five to fifteen percent. Nothing about their strength changed. What changed is that the dip let their tendons load up like a spring and hand that energy back, and those same elastic tissues are what quietly lower the cost of every stride when you use them well.

Jason breaks down where this "inner spring" actually lives in your body, why the same mechanism you see in a golfer's backswing shows up in your forward stride, and how learning to load it turns your skating from something you grind out into something that blends effortlessly into your cross-unders, shuffles, and the ten-and-two movements you see McDavid flow through constantly. Watch the full breakdown to see how to find your inner spring and stop leaving free speed on the ice.

videos.title: Most Coaches Make This Power Skating Mistake
videos.summary_source_text:
Most Coaches Make This Power Skating Mistake The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Is Longevity a Lie?
videos.summary_source_text:
Is Longevity a Lie? Is longevity a big lie?

The idea is simple: eat well, exercise, manage your stress, have good relationships... and you'll live to 100.

The problem is, that's not what the data show.

The New England Centenarian Study, one of the best studies we have on people who actually make it to 100, found that exceptional longevity is largely genetic. You really do need to win the genetic lottery.

What's even weirder is that plenty of centenarians smoked, drank, never exercised, and lived pretty normal lives. They don't avoid heart disease, cancer, or dementia. They just tend to get them later than everyone else. Their genes seem to buy them another decade.

That's why I think the longevity movement is a little misleading.

What we're really talking about is healthspan.

Exercise, good nutrition, sleep, and stress management probably won't turn you into a centenarian. But they can absolutely help you stay stronger, healthier, and more independent for the years you do have. Is longevity a big lie?
